title: Forerunner 965, 265, 265S: Everything to know about Garmin’s first AMOLED display-toting running watches in India
summary: Garmin has launched its first AMOLED display running watches in India, including the Forerunner 965, 265, and 265S. These watches offer extensive tracking features for runners and triathletes, with the 965 boasting advanced mapping and longer battery life. The prices are Rs 67,490 for the Forerunner 965 and Rs 50,490 for the 265 series, and they are available both online and offline.

title: Restaurant Brands earnings beats estimates, fueled by Tim Hortons' and Burger King's strong sales
summary: Restaurant Brands International exceeded Q1 earnings and revenue estimates, driven by double-digit same-store sales growth at Tim Hortons and Burger King. Burger King's U.S. same-store sales climbed 8.7%, indicating a successful turnaround, while Tim Hortons saw a 13.8% increase, especially strong in Canada. Popeyes also contributed with 5.6% same-store sales growth, and Firehouse Subs grew by 6.1%.

title: 3M laying off 1,100 at Maplewood headquarters
summary: 3M is laying off 1,100 employees at its Maplewood headquarters, which represents 10% of its local workforce and is part of a larger global cost-cutting initiative. This follows an earlier announcement of 6,000 global job cuts and an additional 2,500 manufacturing job reductions, bringing the total workforce reduction to 10% worldwide. Economists suggest these layoffs signal broader economic impacts from the Fed's interest rate hikes and changes in fiscal stimulus.

title: Keysight Highlights Challenges, Opportunities in Satellite Industry
summary: Keysight Technologies commissioned a survey revealing software test automation as a top challenge in the satellite industry, alongside the shift from large GEO to smaller LEO satellites due to reduced launch costs. The article discusses how automation in design-to-manufacturing and operational control systems can address these challenges, driven by a "gold rush" mentality and shortened development cycles. Keysight aims to support customers throughout the satellite lifecycle, from design to operations, through various testing, emulation, and simulation tools.

title: IBM CEO Arvind Krishna warns employees who work remotely: 'Your career does suffer'
summary: IBM CEO Arvind Krishna stated that while he is not forcing employees back to the office, those who work remotely may find their careers suffering, particularly regarding promotions into managerial roles. He emphasized that in-person interaction is beneficial for career development and that remote work is best suited for specific individual contributor roles. Krishna's comments contribute to the ongoing debate about the merits of remote versus in-person work, with IBM encouraging employees to come into the office three days a week.

title: 40 Under 40: Champions of Construction 2022
summary: This article celebrates Autodesk's 40 Under 40: Champions of Construction for 2022, highlighting 40 individuals who are making significant contributions to the construction industry through innovation, leadership, and digital transformation. It details their roles, achievements, and impact on their respective companies and the broader AEC sector. The honorees are recognized for advancing digital maturity, implementing new technologies, and fostering collaborative and sustainable practices.

title: DXC Technology migrates insurance marketplace Lloyd’s to new data center
summary: DXC Technology has successfully migrated Lloyd's, the insurance marketplace, to a new, more modern data center as part of Lloyd's 'Blueprint Two' modernization strategy. This complex migration involved moving 70 billion rows of data, 700 IT assets, and over 200 mission-critical applications from a 40-year-old mainframe environment. The move, which took place over a single weekend in February, involved extensive planning and collaboration with over a dozen partners to minimize disruption.

title: Amazon class action alleges Prime subscribers pay false discount prices
summary: Amazon is facing a class action lawsuit alleging that its advertised Amazon Prime discounts are not genuine. The plaintiff claims that Amazon inflates original prices to create the appearance of a discount, thereby misleading consumers. The lawsuit seeks damages for affected customers and alleges violations of FTC guidelines regarding price comparisons.

title: Amazon Prime Subscribers Do Not Get the ‘Exclusive Savings’ They’re Promised, Class Action Alleges [DISMISSED]
summary: A class action lawsuit alleging that Amazon Prime subscribers do not receive promised "exclusive savings" has been dismissed. The judge ruled that the plaintiff failed to demonstrate how Amazon broke its promise or that he incurred damages, noting he did receive a discount on a television. The lawsuit claimed Amazon used "fictitious" strike-through prices by artificially raising product prices before applying "discounts" for Prime members.

title: Goop, Lemme Among Co. Hit With FTC Notices Over Marketing
summary: The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has issued notices to over 600 companies, including Goop and Kourtney Kardashian’s Lemme, Inc., warning them against making unsubstantiated product claims. The FTC stresses the importance of reliable evidence for marketing claims, particularly regarding health or safety benefits, and threatens civil penalties up to $50,120 per violation for deceptive practices. This action follows a Supreme Court decision limiting the FTC's ability to seek equitable monetary relief, prompting the agency to use penalty offense authority as an alternative enforcement tool.

title: Promotional home environment dinks Cornerstone Brand sales
summary: Qurate Retail Inc.'s Cornerstone division experienced a 13% decline in revenue to $297 million in Q1 due to an increasingly promotional environment for home goods and reduced average selling prices. The QxH division (QVC U.S. and HSN) also saw a 5% revenue decline, attributed to fewer customers and weakened consumer sentiment. The company is implementing initiatives to reactivate customer groups, but expects the impact to take several quarters to materialize.

title: Hanumakonda: KTR inaugurates 4 new companies; IT sector hired 1.5L people last year
summary: Telangana's IT and Industries Minister K.T. Rama Rao inaugurated four new IT companies in Hanamkonda (LTI Mindtree, Genpact, HRH Next, and Hexad Solutions Pvt. Ltd.), encouraging local youth for employment and entrepreneurship. Hyderabad continues to be a major IT hub, attracting global companies and adding over 1.5 lakh jobs in 2021-22, with plans to expand IT growth to other districts like Mahabubnagar, Siddipet, Nizamabad, and Nalgonda. The state government's policy framework, infrastructure, and human capital access have made Hyderabad a preferred destination for IT companies.

title: Cantaloupe Launches Smart Technology for Grab And Go at Self-Service Environments
summary: Cantaloupe Inc. has launched Cantaloupe Go, a new line of self-service apps and kiosks that utilize artificial intelligence for purchases in self-service retail locations and micro-markets. The technology allows consumers to unlock coolers or micro-markets and pay for items using a mobile app or kiosk, with AI and sensors tracking purchases. Cantaloupe Go is designed for flexibility in various environments, including food and beverage vending, and can be customized with convenience items.

title: Is the Market Reacting Too Negatively to Pinterest Earnings?
summary: Pinterest's stock tumbled 25% despite beating Q1 2023 top and bottom-line estimates and growing monthly active users (MAUs). The sell-off was primarily driven by concerns over slowing growth, rising operating expenses (opex), and a GAAP net loss of $209 million due to restructuring charges. While analysts remain cautiously optimistic with reiterations, several lowered price targets, reflecting market uncertainty regarding the company's profitability amidst its strategic restructuring efforts.

title: CEO pay continues to soar – new study
summary: A new study by Equilar reveals that median CEO pay at top US public companies increased by 7.7% to a record $22.3 million in 2022, despite negative S&P 500 returns. This rise was primarily driven by stock awards, leading to a median "pay ratio" of 288 times the median employee's compensation, significantly outpacing the 3.6% increase in average US private sector employee earnings. The study highlights a trend of incentivizing executives through substantial stock awards during uncertain economic times.

title: From stores to suppliers, how Destination XL tries to dodge the inventory ‘kiss of death’
summary: Destination XL (DXL) is strategically managing its inventory to avoid overstocking, a common pitfall in retail, by adopting a philosophy of "chasing goods rather than chasing cancellations." The company leverages AI and machine learning for efficient inventory management and has reduced its inventory relative to 2019 levels while increasing turnover. DXL is also diversifying its sourcing geographically, increasing production from Western hemisphere countries like Mexico and Nicaragua, and minimizing reliance on China, while maintaining a finite supplier base to build deeper relationships.

title: IonQ Appoints Pat Tang as VP of Research & Development
summary: IonQ, a quantum computing leader, announced the appointment of Pat Tang as Vice President of Research and Development. Tang, previously an Engineering Vice President at Amazon Lab126 and a team lead at Apple, will lead the company's technical exploration with a focus on developing impactful technologies for IonQ's systems. His extensive experience in building and scaling innovative technologies is expected to be invaluable as IonQ continues to advance quantum computing.

title: GlobalFoundries taps former Amazon exec for CFO seat
summary: GlobalFoundries has appointed former Amazon executive Tim Stone as its new Chief Financial Officer, replacing David Reeder. Stone brings extensive experience from Amazon and previous CFO roles at Snap, Ford Motor, and ASAPP. This leadership change comes as GlobalFoundries reported a 5% year-over-year revenue decline in its first quarter, though the company sees continued growth in markets like automotive and industrial IoT despite broader semiconductor industry challenges.

title: Dillard’s Shoppers Bought Shoes, Cosmetics and Women’s Clothing in Q1
summary: Dillard's Inc. surpassed Wall Street's expectations in Q1 despite a decline in sales and net income, driven by strong performance in cosmetics, shoes, and women's apparel. The company's retail gross margin was 45.6 percent, and operating expenses rose slightly. Analysts suggest that while Dillard's performed well given tough comparisons, the broader retail sector faces challenges due to a pressured middle class and increased spending on experiences.

title: Flush With Federal Money, Strings Attached, a Deep South Factory Votes to Unionize (Published 2023)
summary: Workers at Blue Bird, a Georgia factory producing electric school buses under federal subsidy, voted to unionize with the United Steelworkers. This victory marks a significant win for organized labor and Democrats, who hope federal clean-energy funding will bolster union presence in the South. This is the first major organizing election at a factory receiving federal funds under recent Biden administration legislation aimed at stimulating clean energy and supporting unions.

title: One Giant Leap for Brand Kind
summary: Companies are increasingly engaging in space marketing by placing product logos on spacecraft and conducting stunts in space to promote their brands. This trend is driven by the era of space capitalism and regulatory changes allowing private companies to participate in space missions, offering new revenue streams for financially risky ventures. While some express concern that this commercialization might diminish the sense of wonder surrounding space, brands like Columbia Sportswear believe it can highlight their innovative capabilities and garner publicity, even for failed missions.

title: George Soros bet on railroads, fitness, gig economy and lightened load on Disney, Amazon, dumped Tesla
summary: Soros Fund Management made new investments in railroad operators CSX Corp. and Norfolk Southern Corp., and the gig economy during the first quarter. The fund also adjusted its holdings in the media sector and divested from electric-vehicle maker Tesla Inc. These railroad investments occurred amidst ongoing labor tensions and increased scrutiny over safety in the industry.

title: Layoffs may cause organizational drag: Gartner
summary: According to Gartner research, layoffs can negatively impact shareholder returns within three years by leading to reduced employee morale, increased turnover, and loss of customers, despite initial cost savings. The report highlights that businesses often face immediate costs like severance payments and long-term issues such as higher contractor costs and demands for increased compensation from remaining staff. Gartner suggests alternative cost-cutting measures like voluntary reduced hours, executive pay cuts, hiring freezes, and internal redeployment to avoid "organizational drag."

title: Launch of first TiVo-based TVs delayed to second half of 2023
summary: The launch of the first TiVo-based connected TVs, manufactured by Vestel, has been delayed from spring to the second half of 2023, aligning with the holiday buying season. Despite this delay, Xperi, TiVo's parent company, maintains its revenue guidance for the year and announced a second "top 10" connected TV OEM partner for the European market, with product shipments expected in 2024. Xperi aims to expand this into a global business, emphasizing an independent, unbiased media platform in the competitive smart TV market.

title: Opal Fuels Sees Heavy-Duty Trucking Bulking RNG Demand
summary: Opal Fuels Inc., a major renewable natural gas (RNG) producer and distributor, is expanding its production projects to meet growing demand for RNG as a transportation fuel, particularly from the heavy-duty trucking sector. The company has secured long-term contracts with major corporations like Amazon.com Inc. and UPS, and is developing new landfill-based RNG facilities. Despite a decrease in first-quarter revenue due to holding back renewable identification number (RIN) sales following a drop in RIN prices, Opal Fuels remains optimistic about the future of RNG in the heavy-duty fuel market, projecting significant growth by 2030 and beyond.

title: Cable One® Teams with eero to Launch Advanced Whole-Home Connectivity Solution
summary: Cable One® announced the launch of Wall-To-Wall WiFi, an advanced whole-home connectivity solution, in collaboration with eero, an Amazon company. This service utilizes eero Pro6E and Wi-Fi 6 technology with patented TrueMesh to provide fast, reliable, and secure internet coverage throughout the home, eliminating dead zones and supporting over 100 connected devices simultaneously. The offering includes advanced online security features, parental controls, and an eero Plus option for additional protection.

title: Galileo Financial Technologies Joins AWS Marketplace
summary: Galileo Financial Technologies, a leading fintech company owned by SoFi Technologies, announced its solutions are now available on AWS Marketplace. This move aims to provide clients with innovative and accessible financial technology solutions, streamlining procurement and billing processes while offering Galileo's powerful API platform for card issuing and payment processing. The offerings include transaction processing, a payment risk platform, and conversational AI technology Cyberbank Konecta.

title: Amazon Bulls, Take Note: The Company's Improving Its Operations
summary: Amazon's stock is up 29% for the year due to improvements in its operations, particularly its delivery network, which has cut costs and shipment times. The company plans to expand same-day delivery centers to further enhance efficiency and profitability. Traders can leverage Amazon's performance using specialized ETFs like AMZU for bullish bets and AMZD for bearish positions.

title: Cognizant Strengthens its Global Delivery Network with New Innovation Hub in Malaysia
summary: Cognizant has opened a new regional innovation hub in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, aiming to strengthen its global delivery network and expand its talent pool to 5,000 employees by 2026. This hub features Cognizant’s first ASEAN Innovation Experience Lab and Centres of Excellence, including a Global Quality Engineering and Assurance Centre and an AWS Centre of Excellence, to provide innovative digital solutions to clients. Malaysian officials highlighted the investment as a testament to Malaysia's business environment and its role as a digital hub for ASEAN.

title: A2Z Smart Technologies Corp. announces formation of dedicated Big Data team
summary: A2Z Smart Technologies Corp. has formed a dedicated Big Data team to develop tools for identifying, mining, and collecting data from its Cust2Mate smart cart platform. This initiative aims to monetize data-based services as a significant revenue source. Additionally, A2Z announced a new partnership with HaStok Concept, an Israeli home design chain, expanding its smart cart solution into a new retail vertical.

title: Aramark Sports + Entertainment Announces Latest Innovation with Launch of New Amazon One Age Verification Capability at Coors Field
summary: Aramark Sports + Entertainment has announced the launch of a new Amazon One age verification capability at Coors Field. This innovation aims to streamline the purchasing process for age-restricted products, enhancing customer experience and operational efficiency. The integration signifies Aramark's commitment to leveraging technology for improved service delivery in sports and entertainment venues.

title: What you need to know about Temu, the online shopping app dominating download charts
summary: Online shopping app Temu, owned by Chinese company PDD Holdings Inc., has quickly risen to popularity in Canada with its aggressive marketing, low prices, and gamified shopping experience. While it offers bargain deals, experts caution consumers about product quality, potential environmental impact from shipping and returns, and data privacy concerns given its sister app's issues. The platform's "growth-at-all-costs" approach and referral schemes are disrupting the e-commerce market, leading to a "race to the bottom" that could hurt local businesses.

title: Is BULZ Stock a buy?
summary: The article discusses BULZ, the ticker symbol for the MicroSectors FANG & Innovation 3X Leveraged ETNs, which trades on NYSE Arca. It explains that BULZ is an unsecured debt security providing leveraged exposure to the Solactive FANG Innovation Index, tracking 15 large-cap US tech stocks, and is not suitable for "buy and hold" investments. The article also mentions Bank of Montreal as the issuer and highlights Barclays' recent decision to redeem some of its own ETNs due to past issues, noting this does not directly impact BULZ but provides context on the ETN market.

title: Japan Airlines
summary: Japan Airlines (JAL) partnered with IBM Consulting to digitally transform its financial systems using SAP S/4HANA, overcoming pandemic challenges with a 100% remote deployment. This modernization allowed JAL to enhance operational efficiency, streamline processes, and gain deeper financial insights, despite significant market disruption. The project resulted in a 60% reduction in SAP customizations and improved financial reporting and analysis capabilities.

title: Invesco BulletShares 2031 Corporate Bond ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NASDAQ:BSCV)
summary: The Invesco BulletShares 2031 Corporate Bond ETF (BSCV) invests primarily in investment-grade corporate bonds maturing in 2031, aiming to return capital and proceeds to investors upon unwinding in December 2031. The ETF, managed by Invesco, had assets under management of $1.59 billion and a dividend yield of 4.60% as of the article's publication. Its shares have seen a slight increase year-to-date and its top holdings include major corporations like Verizon, Oracle, and Amazon.

title: TUG Top Holdings List & Exposure (STF Tactical Growth ETF)
summary: This article provides a detailed list of the top holdings for the STF Tactical Growth ETF (TUG), highlighting its significant exposure to technology companies like NVIDIA, Apple, and Microsoft. It also breaks down TUG's geographic, currency, sector, and industry exposures, showing a strong concentration in the United States and the technology sector, particularly in semiconductors. The fund is described as a multi-asset allocation fund focusing on North America.

title: Amazon Drivers Avoid Arbitration Claiming Non-delivery of Updated TOS
summary: The Ninth Circuit denied Amazon's motion to compel arbitration in a case brought by Amazon Flex drivers, ruling that the 2016 Terms of Service (TOS) applied instead of the 2019 version. Amazon failed to prove it provided adequate notice of the updated 2019 TOS and that there was mutual assent to its arbitration agreement. This decision highlights the importance for companies to ensure broad arbitration provisions and maintain records of notice for TOS updates.

title: In The Multicloud World, The Data’s The Thing
summary: Dell is expanding its Apex as-a-service portfolio, particularly focusing on data as the immutable center of the multicloud environment. The company emphasizes that while applications are ephemeral, data persistence and accessibility across various public and on-premises clouds are crucial for enterprises. Dell is positioning its storage-as-a-service offerings as a "Switzerland" for data, enabling organizations to achieve data gravity and avoid vendor lock-in, a strategy that executive John Roese states is paying off and differentiating Dell from competitors.

title: Activist firm Jana eyes boardroom fight at Freshpet
summary: Activist investor Jana Partners, the largest shareholder in pet food company Freshpet, wants to replace four board members to improve capital expenditure supervision and position the company for a potential sale. Jana, which owns a 9.3% stake, criticized the board for failing to oversee management and allowing performance to decline. Freshpet's shares have experienced significant volatility, and Jana's push comes amidst consolidation in the pet food industry.

title: ETF of the Week: Goldman Sachs Hedge Industry VIP ETF (GVIP)
summary: VettaFi’s Tom Lydon discusses the Goldman Sachs Hedge Industry VIP ETF (GVIP) which offers exposure to top holdings favored by hedge funds without an overweight toward any single stock. GVIP provides diversification across various companies, including some mid-cap and international stocks, making it a less volatile option for investors seeking innovative companies. It provides a consensus of top companies chosen by leading hedge fund managers, appealing to investors looking for strong, well-vetted companies.

title: Local Bounti names new CEO in executive transition
summary: Local Bounti Corporation announced that Anna Fabrega, former Freshly CEO and Amazon executive, will become CEO of the company on June 5, 2023. Current Co-CEOs and Co-Founders, Craig Hurlbert and Travis Joyner, will transition to Senior Vice President of Strategy and Chief Technology Officer, respectively, while retaining their board seats. Fabrega brings over two decades of experience in operations, consumer goods, and food production, with a proven track record of scaling businesses, including leading Amazon Go.

title: New HP and Sonos Devices Accentuate the Ultimate Home Office Workstation
summary: This article reviews the HP E45c G5 DQHD Curved Monitor and Sonos Era 100 Speakers, highlighting how they enhance productivity in a home office setup. The author praises the monitor's ultrawide display and Device Bridge feature for seamless multi-system operation, and the Sonos speakers for their superior sound quality and easy integration. Both devices are presented as valuable investments for improving the efficiency and enjoyment of hybrid work environments.

title: ETF of the Week: Goldman Sachs Hedge Industry VIP ETF (GVIP)
summary: The Goldman Sachs Hedge Industry VIP ETF (GVIP) is highlighted as the ETF of the Week. GVIP provides exposure to top stock picks from hedge funds, focusing on a consensus of leading managers rather than an overweighting of individual stocks. The ETF diversifies holdings across large-cap, mid-cap, and international companies, offering a less volatile way for investors to participate in innovative companies.

title: US: Local Bounti appoints Anna Fabrega as CEO
summary: Local Bounti Corporation has announced the appointment of Anna Fabrega, formerly CEO of Freshly and an Amazon executive, as its new CEO, effective June 5, 2023. Current Co-CEOs and Co-Founders, Craig Hurlbert and Travis Joyner, will transition to strategic leadership roles within the company and remain on the Board of Directors. Fabrega brings extensive experience in operations, consumer goods, and food production, with a focus on scaling businesses and expanding market reach.

title: Local Bounti names new CEO
summary: Local Bounti Corp. has announced Anna Fabrega, former Freshly CEO and Amazon executive, will take over as CEO on June 5. The current co-CEOs and co-founders, Craig Hurlbert and Travis Joyner, will transition to senior leadership roles and retain their board seats. Fabrega brings over two decades of experience in operations, consumer goods, and food production to her new role at Local Bounti.

title: Local Bounti names new CEO
summary: Anna Fabrega, formerly CEO of Freshly and an Amazon executive, has been appointed as the new CEO of Local Bounti, effective June 5. The company's co-founders, Craig Hurlbert and Travis Joyner, will transition to senior vice president of strategy and chief technology officer, respectively, while retaining their board seats. Fabrega brings extensive experience in operations, consumer goods, and food production, with a focus on scaling businesses to drive Local Bounti's growth strategy.

title: Amazon Settles With FTC Over Claims Ring Doorbell Spies on Users (AMZN)
summary: Amazon has agreed to pay $30.8 million to settle two privacy cases with the Federal Trade Commission. One case involved allegations that Amazon's Ring video doorbells illegally spied on users, while the other concerned Alexa speakers collecting children's data without consent. The company will pay $5.8 million for the Ring complaint.

title: Netgear Nighthawk M6 Pro Wi-Fi Router Review
summary: The Netgear Nighthawk M6 Pro is a high-performance mobile Wi-Fi router supporting 5G mobile broadband and Wi-Fi 6E, making it suitable for business travelers and remote work. Despite its versatility and robust features like a 13-hour battery life and a 2.5 Gigabit Ethernet port, its high price and somewhat unclear initial setup documentation are notable drawbacks. This review highlights its compact design, strong performance, and ability to switch between networking modes, positioning it as a top-tier but expensive solution for connectivity on the go.
